description: GasLib is a collection of technical gas network descriptions and contract-based nomination data, with gas flows and pressure bounds at entries and exits, meant to promote research on gas network optimisation with large, realistic benchmark instances. It grew out of the research project Technical Capacities of Gas Networks, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Economics and Technology, and is hosted by the Zuse Institute Berlin. The networks are based partly on real data from the German transmission operator Open Grid Europe, distorted so that they differ from the original; the largest instances are GasLib-4197, GasLib-2607, GasLib-582 and GasLib-134, plus smaller test networks and community extensions such as GasLibE-39. Data are XML files for network, compressor station, nomination and combined decision descriptions, each with an XSD schema, plus GAMS mixed-integer nonlinear models, downloadable at no cost. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-3.0. Simulation uses are benchmarking gas network flow and optimisation methods and capacity studies. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
